text:
alex: Heads-up — starting ~11:42 PDT we saw a steady admission queue in us-west-2. API latency + p95 token times spiked. Some pods report 95% GPU utilization while sibling nodes are idle.

janelle: Is this the same symptom as yesterday or new? Any obvious errors in the scheduler logs?

samir: New pattern. Yesterday was preemption churn; this looks like head-of-line blocking in the admission queue. Jobs at head have GPU pin=true and never release slots, so following jobs can't get assigned.

alex: Confirmed — checked pod annotations: a batch of long-lived debug runs were scheduled with gpu_pinning: true and preemptible: false. They hold specific GPU indices.

infra-bot: ALERT: scheduler-pool-gpu queue-length=138, avg-wait=42s, region=us-west-2, severity=warning

maria: Ugh. That flag combined with the new node affinity rule (nodeSelector: nvidia.k8s.io/gpu-type=rtx) causes binding to a subset of GPUs. Effectively reduces the pool size.

janelle: Can we force-unbind the offending pods and reschedule with gpu_pinning=false? Any risk to running jobs?

samir: We can try a graceful drain on the pinned nodes, but some jobs don't checkpoint. Might kill a handful. I can patch the scheduler to ignore gpu_pinning for admission decisions as a stopgap (preferential placement still kept).

alex: Paste of current admission policy snippet:
```
admission:
  max_inflight_per_pool: 1000
  prefer_local: true
  respect_gpu_pinning: true  # <- suspect
  preemption: { enabled: false }
```

maria: If respect_gpu_pinning=true, scheduler refuses to assign other jobs to that GPU even if it could co-locate. That causes head-of-line when the pinned job is single-threaded and slow.

oncall-ops: @samir @janelle assigning high priority to this — customer-facing latency impact. Do we have a quick revert plan?

samir: Plan A (quick): set respect_gpu_pinning=false in k8s-configmap and roll to scheduler replicas (no restart of nodes). Will let scheduler steal placements. Risk: minor locality regression.

Plan B (safe): add an admission override for queue-length>50 to temporarily ignore pinning. Slightly more work but less config churn.

Plan C (nuclear): cordon debug nodes and evict pinned jobs manually. Higher customer risk.

janelle: I prefer Plan B. Can you draft the admission override? Also instrument a metric: pinned_gpus_in_use / total_powered_gpus so we can alert before this happens.

samir: Drafted override rule (will PR):
```
- rule: ignore-pinning-on-saturation
  when: queue_length > 50
  action: admission.allow_if_gpu_available(ignore_pinning=true)
```

alex: Roll this to a single scheduler replica first and monitor.

maria: I'll open a short-lived dashboard: per-node gpu-assignment heatmap, pinned_count, queue_length, preemption_off flag.

oncall-ops: After rollout, notify when p95 latency drops below baseline and queue_length < 30. If not, fallback to Plan A.

samir: Doing the canary now against replica-2. Will post logs.

infra-bot: DEPLOY: scheduler-configmap updated by samir. Canaries: replica-2.

alex: Early signal: queue_length -> 28 within 60s, some previously-idle GPUs now show 20-40% utilization. p95 token latency trending down.

janelle: Nice. Follow-up: let's add an automated rule to convert pin=true jobs that exceed a runtime threshold (eg > 6h) to preemptible=true or move to a reserved pool.

maria: Agreed — longer-term we should also add a placement balancer that rejects extreme affinity constraints when effective capacity < X%.

oncall-ops: Filing incident ticket for postmortem: INC-2026-0423. Assign to @samir for root cause and to @maria for dashboard + mitigation backlog.

samir: Will include timeline, offending job IDs, and a small repro harness. Also add unit tests for admission rule order to prevent this regression.

alex: Thanks team. We'll keep the override live until the placement balancer lands. Ping if it slides back up. :thumbsup:
